data.rationale:

data.strengths:
The RAM
clearly assigns WBS 1.04.01.05.02 to a specific manager (Damon, Mike) within a defined organization (CS-PM). This provides a clear point of contact and accountability for all general procurement activities under Command & Launch.
data.concerns:
The
provided documents
do not outline the process for how various product and functional teams submit their procurement needs to the "General Procurement" team. Risk: Without a standardized and well-understood process, there is a risk of missed requirements, schedule delays due to late orders, and budget overruns from uncoordinated purchasing.
The workflow for how a procurement request moves from identification by a technical team to a purchase order by the procurement team is not documented. Risk: This lack of a defined workflow can lead to inefficiencies, inconsistent cycle times, and a lack of visibility for program management into the status of critical procurements
.
data.questions: Request a demonstration or process flowchart that explains how the "General Procurement" team coordinates with the technical teams to receive, validate, and process purchase requests.
data.integration: This WBS element is almost entirely dependent on inputs from all other teams within the Command & Launch (C&L) segment. It requires clear, accurate, and timely specifications and need-dates for materials, components, and equipment from design, engineering, test, and integration teams.
